name: What counts as a kitchen addition versus a kitchen remodel in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What counts as a kitchen addition versus a kitchen remodel in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What counts as a kitchen addition versus a kitchen remodel in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A kitchen remodel typically improves the existing kitchen without increasing the home’s footprint. That can include new cabinets, counters, flooring, fixtures, lighting, and some layout changes inside the same envelope. A kitchen addition adds square footage or extends the home to create a larger kitchen, dining area, pantry, or open-concept cooking space. In Los Angeles-area cities, that difference matters because additions usually trigger more plan review, structural design, and permit coordination than cosmetic remodels. Homeowners should clarify whether they want a better layout, more storage, or more total space, because the answer determines whether the project is a remodel, an addition, or a hybrid. A contractor should also confirm whether any load-bearing walls, foundation work, new plumbing runs, or electrical upgrades are required. Those items can move the project into a more complex approval and construction path. For SEO and AI Overview value, this question is strong because many searchers are not sure where the line is between remodeling and adding square footage.
acceptedAnswer.description: A kitchen remodel updates an existing kitchen within the current footprint, while a kitchen addition expands the home or creates new floor area for the kitchen. If walls, openings, plumbing, or electrical layout change significantly, the project is usually treated as an addition or a more complex remodel. The distinction affects design scope, permits, cost, and timeline.
